topic: Getting paid on time without losing the client

shorts.title: Get paid without losing the client

scenes.text: Set payment terms in writing before you start. Say due date, how to pay, and any late fee you can lawfully charge.
Invoice straight away. Show what you did, the date, the cost, the due date and the payment terms — no vague one-line bills.
If a client runs late, follow a simple routine: send a reminder two days after the due date, then call after seven days. Keep it polite, firm and factual.
For repeat late payers, use upfront deposits or cash terms, or offer a small early-payment discount for work you can afford to do that way.

If you’re in New Zealand on construction work, remember the Construction Contracts Act payment claim process can force a schedule. Bottom line: written terms, clear invoices, and quick reminders beat chasing later.

visual.text: Written terms and quick reminders win

shorts.caption: Set terms up front, invoice clearly, and use a short reminder routine. If you’re in NZ, the Construction Contracts Act gives a formal route.
